0a65b916927af23d0eeacef453c2fd08cfebfb56: Filzmoos is a small, low-key resort: 20 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where people come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. Filzmoos's family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for getting children started on skiing. Filzmoos's modest altitude, starting at 970 m with the summit at 1591 m, makes it sensitive to climate variations. January and February remain the safest months for optimal snow cover. Outside that window, checking the snow reports before you leave is strongly advised. The budget for a stay in Filzmoos is clearly high: 70€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence, but it's worth being aware of it before you go. In short, Filzmoos doesn't rival the giants of skiing and doesn't pretend to. It's an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.

0ae6cc7d0ce6446c1705d0290f76088122a44dc0: A resort on a human scale, Aussois focuses on friendly service and proximity rather than impressive figures. Its 55 km of runs are ideal for a 3- to 4-day stay, especially for families or skiers who don't need to constantly change their playground. Aussois's family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, a well-run childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It's one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. With a summit at 2,750 m and a village at 1,500 m, snow reliability at Aussois is generally dependable from January to the end of March. A few exceptionally mild winters can cause strain early in the season, but the situation recovers quickly once substantial snowfall arrives. The 41€ day lift pass places Aussois among the mid-range resorts on budget: neither cheap nor exorbitant. The quality of the ski area and facilities justifies the price for most skiers. In short: Aussois is one of those rare resorts that combines a genuine village, a sincere family atmosphere and runs suited to everyone. It's hard to have a bad stay here.
